brief: Goldman's monthly crypto on-chain and market update: BTC opened September near $79K, fell to $75K mid-month as the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate, then broke the $82K level that had held since August and, after absorbing both the CLARITY setback and a Fed rate hike, hit a new high of $87.3K before settling near $84K (+6.4% MoM). ETH and SOL also rose (+8.9%, +14.6%) on the same breakout, with BTC/ETH/SOL spot ETFs taking in $2.4bn/$634mm/$262mm respectively, though all three faded into month-end despite the inflows. BTC has already cleared $86.5K in early October, and the note cites October as BTC's seasonally strongest month (mean +15.4%, MarketView) as the setup turns benign but fragile: the Fed-hike debate has slipped to December while energy, long-end yields and AI-debt issuance stay live risks. Separately, CLARITY's failed September 15 Senate vote pushed the SEC and CFTC to fill the gap: the SEC issued a five-year tokenized-equities exemption, a custody proposal and buyback/staking guidance, while the CFTC eased broker registration and updated tokenized money-market and blockchain recordkeeping guidance. On-chain activity across the three networks was mixed.
